bio: Molly is a producer, digital strategist, tinkerer, and occasional writer. She helps projects find their shape — by trade she gets things made, for pleasure she makes them. Over a decade in San Francisco doing very San Francisco things: employee twelve at a scrappy startup, ad agency life, global digital campaigns at Apple, getting scolded by AI. You can currently find her working on notion.com.

personas.label: Producing
personas.name: Producer
personas.headline: Getting dots in a row
personas.blurb: Turning a big vague idea into a crisp plan—and then actually shipping it.
personas.longVersion: Molly takes big, vague ideas and gives them a point of view, a plan, and somewhere to be on Tuesday. She’s spent 10+ years helping creative and technical teams turn strategy into shipped work. Currently doing all that at notion.com.

personas.label: Writing
personas.name: Writer
personas.headline: Occasionally interesting
personas.blurb: Writing in hopes of turning fog and broken glass into chewing gum.
personas.longVersion: Writing for websites, yes—but also about movies, memories, fake deadlines, the very specific feeling of listening to a podcast in damp woods, and the private thrill of getting one sentence exactly right.
bullets: Briefs and strategy docs that mean something

personas.label: Making things
personas.name: Crafter

personas.blurb: Making something small and slightly impractical, probably as a gift, probably unfinished.
personas.longVersion: Building a tiny empire of impractical side quests: retro websites, dramatic monologues, self-portraits, block printing, tarot-card mosaics, and whatever the craft goblin demands next.
bullets: Hand-made books with wobbly bindings

personas.label: Keeping up
personas.name: Pop Culture Expert
personas.headline: Extremely, unapologetically online
personas.blurb: Knows what happened, why it happened, and which group chat called it first.
personas.longVersion: Letterboxd opinions, reality TV analysis, celebrity-media brain rot, and just enough academia to make the gossip dangerous. Watch her follow a meme to its source, a scandal to its framing, and a throwaway headline to the larger cultural sickness.
